create.title: Tao--Trudgian--Yang reciprocal exponent-pair wedge
create.statement_tex: Let D=X^delta, L=X^ell in the active M2 triangle, and assume the denominator block has sup_d |w_D(d)|+sum_d |w_D(d+1)-w_D(d)| << 1 uniformly. The Tao--Trudgian--Yang exponent pair (89/1282,997/1282), applied after conjugating the reciprocal phase to the sigma=2 model phase, gives |B_L(D;X)| <<_epsilon X^([89(1+ell)+819delta]/1282+epsilon). Hence the X^(1/4+epsilon) target holds when 178ell+1638delta<=463. This covers every frequency through delta<=1015/3632 and a nonempty lower slice through delta<=463/1638.
create.next_action: Write and verify the actual normalized-BV dyadic and endpoint profiles, then use this wedge as proved M2 coverage. Do not extend it to arbitrary bounded weights.

create.title: Exact Round-5 frequency coverage and residual corridor
create.statement_tex: In Omega={(delta,ell):1/4<=delta<=1/2, 0<=ell<=delta-1/4}, the elementary T2S, full second-derivative, and trivial estimates cover the terminal line ell=delta-1/4 and the point (1/2,0) at target 1/4. Under the normalized-BV transfer for the TTY pair, the additional wedge is 178ell+1638delta<=463. The exact remaining set is U={(delta,ell) in Omega: 0<=ell<delta-1/4 and 178ell+1638delta>463} minus {(1/2,0)}.
create.next_action: Target only the explicit residual corridor U. Keep the fixed-profile BV hypothesis separate from arbitrary bounded-weight statements.

create.title: Exact two-shift sine kernel and bounded-weight D/L sharpness
create.statement_tex: The rho=1,3 shifts are exactly an odd-frequency parity projector. Pairing positive and negative frequencies gives S_(2,L)=4 sum_(d asymp D) w_D(d) chi_4(r_d) sum_(h>0 odd) a_(h,H,L) sin(pi h(X-dr_d)/(2d)), where r_d is a nearest odd integer to X/d. The kernel vanishes at X=dr_d but has constant size on |X-dr_d| asymp D/L. For some X asymp Y there is a bounded nonnegative sparse denominator weight with actual Vaaler amplitudes for which |S_(2,L)| >> D/L. Thus no improvement of T2S is uniform over arbitrary bounded weights; the example has variation >>D/L and does not obstruct a fixed normalized-BV profile.
create.next_action: Exploit the actual fixed normalized-BV denominator profile or chi_4(r_d) oscillation. Do not seek cancellation by pairing the two shifts, and do not claim a bound uniform over arbitrary bounded weights.

create.title: Smooth Poisson duality and equivalent three-quarter target
create.statement_tex: For a fixed W in C_c^infinity((a,b)), d-Poisson summation and uniform stationary phase give sum_d W(d/D)e(hX/(4d)) = e(1/8)(hX)^(1/4)/2 sum_(k>=1) W(sqrt(hX/(4kD^2))) k^(-3/4)e(sqrt(hXk))+O_W(1). With K=XL/D^2 and M=LK, the positive M2 block equals -e(1/8)/(2pi) X^(1/4)M^(-3/4) T_(L,K)+O_W(1), where T_(L,K)=sum_(h asymp L,k asymp K) chi_4(h)a_(L,K)(h,k)e(sqrt(Xhk)) has the actual smooth slanted symbol. Therefore T_(L,K)<<M^(3/4)X^epsilon is equivalent-hard to the smooth positive block target, not an easier reduction.
create.next_action: Prove the signed M^(3/4) product-phase estimate only in a genuinely new part of the residual corridor, or exploit the actual fixed-profile sine kernel instead. Do not apply unweighted derivative estimates after grouping by m=hk.

create.title: Diagonal-critical dual square-root spacing mean square
create.statement_tex: For K>=L and the actual normalized smooth symbol a_(L,K), prove sum_(h asymp L) |sum_(k asymp K) a_(L,K)(h,k)e(sqrt(Xhk))|^2 <<_epsilon L^(1/2)K^(3/2)X^epsilon. This implies the dual M^(3/4) target after Cauchy, but is stronger because Cauchy erases chi_4(h); it is exactly diagonal-critical when K=L, corresponding to D=X^(1/2).
create.next_action: Audit square-root spacing and large-sieve inputs at K>=L. Prefer a signed estimate retaining chi_4(h), since the mean-square target is stronger and has no endpoint slack.
